route.name: Binder BR_TRANSACTION receive to generic target stub
flow: BinderInvoker::OnTransaction reads a fixed-size binder_transaction_data[_secctx] and rejects a null frame
BinderInvoker::Transaction ParseFrom(data buffer, data_size), checks non-null offsets when offsets_size > 0, then InjectOffsets

candidate_review.rationale: The receive-to-dispatch path is source-supported, but this bounded review did not establish a concrete unvalidated caller-controlled field reaching a memory or security-sensitive sink. Do not infer device impact or claim a whole-tree zero-finding result.
control_and_counterevidence: OnTransaction reads only the fixed transaction-header size through Parcel::ReadBuffer and returns an invalid-data error on null.

BinderInvoker::UnflattenObject checks Parcel offsets, requires a full flat_binder_object through ReadBuffer, dispatches only BINDER_TYPE_BINDER or BINDER_TYPE_HANDLE, and checks local BINDER cookies with IPCProcessSkeleton::IsContainsObject before reuse.
MessageParcel::ReadRawData rejects size zero and requires the parcel-declared size to equal the requested size; large-data path checks AshmemGetSize(fd) >= requested size before mmap.

IPCObjectStub dispatch has previously reviewed special transaction branches; this review concerns the generic BR_TRANSACTION receive/Parcel boundary and did not identify a new specialized transaction effect.
candidate_review.reachability_and_effect: Caller supplies transaction Parcel contents through Binder, but the Binder driver mediates transaction buffers, object offsets, handles, and transferred FDs. This scout did not re-verify kernel-driver validation and makes no claim about malformed driver output. No specific ordinary-app security effect was established.
candidate_review.authorization: No per-transaction access-control claim was inferred from this generic receive path; service-specific authorization belongs to individual OnRemoteRequest implementations and was outside this one-route review.

findings: T18 independently matched all three pinned IPC source identities above to the local checkout.

T18 examined the UnFlattenDBinderObject special BINDER_TYPE_PTR branch. Public MessageParcel::ReadRemoteObject enters Parcel::ReadObject, which checks offsets and parcel object size before unmarshalling; UnflattenObject repeats offset and fixed-size object checks, validates object type, and checks local binder cookie membership.

For a valid BINDER_TYPE_PTR object offset, Binder-driver validation and receiver pointer conversion are relevant external controls. The driver source is not part of the communication_ipc pin and was not bound in this review; no vulnerability is inferred from it.
No generic authorization gate is claimed. Authorization for ordinary transaction codes is service-specific in OnRemoteRequest implementations, outside this bounded route review.

independent_review.verdict: 0 new candidates; the apparent pre-CheckOffsets DBinder buffer dereference is blocked on the normal MessageParcel::ReadRemoteObject API path, subject to product dependency version binding.
facts: MessageParcel::ReadRemoteObject calls Parcel::ReadObject<IRemoteObject>; Parcel::ReadObject runs CheckOffsets before unmarshalling and requires an exact current offset and enough bytes for a parcel_flat_binder_object.
UnflattenObject later checks offsets again, reads a complete flat object, dispatches known object types, and checks local BINDER cookie ownership.
Binder driver behavior is an external dependency and was not treated as verified from the IPC pin.

These are method-level and do not establish full Binder-driver integration coverage. No tests run this turn.
